clue.text: Unusual story about English shellfish

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
unusual tells us the letters of story come out in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: An odd tale told about an English shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges STORY to OYSTR, and 'about' wraps that round E to give the shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: This bivalve mollusc is a shellfish prized for eating and pearls.

clue.text: Gastronome let television chef include egg dish

indicators.note: the words of the clue include, inside their run of letters, the dish being sought

explanation.surface: A food lover lets a TV cook make an egg dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word breaks of 'gastrOnOME LET TElevision', signalled by 'include'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten eggs fried flat in a pan make this classic dish.

clue.text: Sweetheart obtains best crystallised fruit

parts.note: sugar is an affectionate term for a sweetheart
a plum job or role is the best one

explanation.surface: A lover gets the finest candied fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat of fruit boiled in syrup is the traditional sense of this term, as in the Christmas story.

clue.text: Fish sleep upside down, quietly dropping off

indicators.note: dropping off says a letter is removed from the turned word
in a down clue, upside down means the word sleep is read from bottom to top

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A fish sleeps belly-up and quietly nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upside down' turns SLEEP into PEELS, and 'dropping off' removes P (quietly) to leave the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are snake-like fish found in rivers and seas.

clue.text: Clergyman reverts to opening wine

indicators.note: reverts tells us the abbreviation for a clergyman runs backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title
a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A vicar returns to the start of his wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverts' turns REV into VER, followed by MOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortified wine flavoured with herbs, drunk as an aperitif or in cocktails.

clue.text: Starts to eat my bananas and cheese

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, mental

explanation.surface: Begin eating my bananas and cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss cheese with large holes, made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Cook sent in more soup

indicators.note: to cook figures or accounts is to falsify them, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A chef is told to send more soup in.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick Italian vegetable soup with pasta or rice.

clue.text: Taking advantage of some of those famous in Greece

indicators.note: some of says only part of the letter run of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Exploiting part of Greece's celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploiting something is employing it for your benefit.

clue.text: Central European country has no one without food

indicators.note: has no says a letter is missing from the country's name

parts.note: Hungary lies in central Europe
a means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A nation in central Europe is left with nobody to feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being starved means wanting a meal.

clue.text: Odds on something very cold for seasoning

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds when a race begins
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: A bet placed on something chilled for flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price in betting, the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: A spice is an aromatic flavouring such as pepper or cinnamon.

clue.text: Drink and get very excited after some breakfast

indicators.note: after places the word for getting excited behind the breakfast item

parts.note: an egg is one item of a breakfast
to flip is to lose one's composure

explanation.surface: A breakfast drink that gets someone worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot drink of beer or spirits beaten with egg and sugar.

clue.text: Refer to chaps on it regrouping

parts.note: chaps means men

indicators.note: regrouping says the letters of on it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men are told to refer to it while they regroup.
explanation.definitionFit: To name something in passing is to cite it.

clue.text: An aristocrat before his time, almost

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A nobleman arrives a little ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A British nobleman ranking above viscount and below marquess.

clue.text: Freezing what comes from canes for cake decoration

parts.note: icing is the forming of ice, freezing
sugar is extracted from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Cold stuff from the cane fields used on cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Finely powdered sweetener used for frosting cakes.

clue.text: A long hybrid fruit from trailing prickly plant

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so the letters of a long are mixed

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: A long fruit bred as a cross from a creeping bramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' rearranges A LONG into LOGAN; the definition is the plant, the answer is also a hybrid fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble cross of raspberry and blackberry with thorny trailing canes.

clue.text: Time to authorise fat for candles

parts.note: to allow is to authorise or permit

explanation.surface: It's time to permit fat for candle-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered animal fat once used to make candles and soap.

clue.text: Possibly oxygen-O-will provide heat for cooking

parts.note: oxygen is one example of a gas
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Oxygen and the letter O will cook dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: O is read by its shape, a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A burner on a hob fuelled by gas, used to heat pans.

clue.text: Very pleasant-tasting substance in English peach

parts.note: nectar is a delicious drink, the drink of the gods

explanation.surface: A delicious juice inside an English peach.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of the peach.

clue.text: Shift gear, give distress

indicators.note: shift means move about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Change gear and cause upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to grieve or wrong them.

clue.text: Get away with half of loaf inside breaded veal

indicators.note: inside places the half-word within the word for getting away

parts.note: to escape is to get away

indicators.note: half of takes the first two letters of loaf

explanation.surface: Make off with half a loaf inside a veal cutlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of meat, often veal, coated in crumbs and fried.

clue.text: Ban half of them before boozer has to leave

indicators.note: half of takes the latter two letters of them

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Half of them are banned from the pub before they have to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition, especially on trade.

clue.text: Criticises buffets

explanation.surface: Criticises buffets.
explanation.definitionFit: Running down someone's work is criticising; buffets as a verb means blows or strikes.

clue.text: A piece of timber on ship

parts.note: a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: A plank of wood loaded on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a vessel or vehicle is being on board it.

clue.text: Male amateur rider makes piles

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a rider is an addition to a document, a postscript, PS

explanation.surface: A man who rides as an amateur makes stacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is not a horseman: it is an addendum, PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots or piles are large quantities.

clue.text: Complaint about food rejected: it's food

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the two words before it are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A grumble about food sent back: it's still food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the pair of words before it around as one run; the definition 'it's food' reads as a wry comment on the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of minced meat served in a bun.

clue.text: Genuine, unbounded, awful boredom

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the remaining letters are rearranged
unbounded means the outer letters of genuine are lost

explanation.surface: Real, limitless, terrible boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless weariness from lack of interest is a French-derived word for tedium.

clue.text: Party girl needs one

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a means one

explanation.surface: A party girl needs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive occasion or celebration is a gala.

clue.text: Cheese is not long cut

indicators.note: cut says the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: brief means short, not long

explanation.surface: This cheese isn't sliced for long.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cow's-milk cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Racecourse area in bay perhaps

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: A racecourse set in a bay on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' is not a coastal inlet but the bay laurel; AINTREE, near Liverpool, hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merseyside course that stages the Grand National horse race.

clue.text: Left one to take care of covered entrance

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: Someone left behind to look after a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed porch supported by columns at a building's front.

clue.text: Milk suppliers dry mine with a special formula

indicators.note: a special formula is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are remixed

explanation.surface: Dairy farmers dry out a mine using a special recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who keep cows and deliver their product to customers.

clue.text: Cut English? That's hard

parts.note: to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: Is English being cut? That's tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh or strict treatment is hard to bear.
